chapter: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
title: Preferring Estes Park, Longmont and Fort Collins audiences to Denver's
summary: He chooses to drive to resort and nearby towns where audiences appreciate the band more than Denver crowds, who stare at him.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: I chose to play the surrounding areas, which seem to me -- which not only seem to me, which is a fact, like up in Estes Park for the past three seasons. I've been playing there summer and winter because of the fact that it is a resort town where we get people from all the states. It seems like they appreciate the band more, you know. Are they more hip or are they just more hungry for that type of music? Same way with a little town of Longmont, and Loveland and Fort Collins and places. They seem to just be more hip than Denver, you know?
So this is why I've been a little reluctant, as I said before, to just play,-- and this is at home.

But I'd rather drive the extra miles, even in the wintertime, to play for people that appreciate what you're offering, more so than to sit up and play for an audience here that stares at you while you're playing,
and they look at you like you started a world war, you know? (Laughter) Right.
This is the thing that happens here, you know, in Denver.
